explainTr: Okul kurallarında uzun cümlecikler kısaltılır. 'Students who run in the hall' yerine 'Students running in the hall' denir. Aktif anlam için -ing (present participle) kullanılır: students arriving late, the woman sitting there.

Edilgen anlam için V3 (past participle) kullanılır: 'Forms that are submitted late' yerine 'Forms submitted late'. Kural: who/which + be fiilini at, geriye kalanı bırak. Fiil edilgense V3, etkinse -ing kalır.

Dikkat: Cümle başında da kullanılır: Walking into the room, she saw a note. Ama bu yapıda özne, eylemi gerçekten yapan kişi olmalı. Ayrıca sürekli tekrarlanan eylemler için de olur: Students using phones in class will be warned.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'geç gelen öğrenciler' ve 'geç teslim edilen ödevler' gibi sıfat-fiil yapıları (-en / -len) kullanırız. İngilizcede bunun karşılığı -ing (etken) ve V3 (edilgen): students arriving late, homework submitted late.

reading.title: The Student Handbook
reading.text:
Hafsa spent Saturday morning reading the Maple Grove Student Handbook. Mr. Brown had told her that a substitute teacher must know the main rules, because students often test new adults. The handbook was long, but the rules were clearly organized, and Hafsa made notes in the margin.

The first section covered arrival and attendance. Students arriving after the 8:15 bell must sign in at the front office and take a late pass to class. Parents dropping off children should use the side lane, since cars parked in the bus zone block traffic. Absences are excused only when a note, signed by a parent, reaches the office within three days.

The second section dealt with behavior in the building. Students walking in the hallways must stay on the right and keep their voices low. Anyone caught running will be asked to return to the start and walk again. Backpacks left in the hallway will be moved to the lost-and-found box, and items not claimed within a month will be donated.

Technology was the most detailed part. Cell phones brought to school must stay in lockers or backpacks during class time. A phone seen during a lesson will be taken to the office, where a parent can pick it up after school. For tests, there is a stricter rule: any device found on a desk is treated as cheating, and the test will not be counted. Students using school laptops must follow the same guidelines and may visit only websites approved by the teacher.

The last section explained consequences. A first violation usually results in a warning, followed by a call to the parents. Repeated problems can lead to detention or, in serious cases, a short suspension decided by the principal. Hafsa noticed that the handbook also listed rewards: students praised by teachers earn points, and classes showing excellent behavior receive a pizza party.

She closed the handbook and smiled. The rules were strict, but they were also fair and predictable, and that made her work as a substitute easier to imagine.

writing.promptTr: Bir sınıf için velilere kısa bir kural duyurusu yaz. En az üç kısaltılmış cümlecik kullan (students arriving..., homework handed in..., devices seen...). 120-180 kelime yaz.
writing.promptEn: Write a short letter to parents explaining classroom rules. Use at least three participle clauses.
writing.model: Dear parents, I would like to explain a few classroom rules for this semester. Students arriving after the bell must sign the late list by the door. Homework handed in after Friday will lose five points, so please check the planner every evening. Phones brought to school should stay in backpacks during lessons, and devices seen on a desk will be taken to the office. Students working in groups must keep their voices low, and anyone disturbing others will receive a warning. Books borrowed from the class library should be returned within two weeks. Children following these rules will earn stickers, and classes showing excellent behavior will enjoy a movie on Friday afternoon. I believe that clear rules make everyone feel safe and respected. If you have any questions about the guidelines, please contact me at the school office. I am always happy to explain the reasons behind a rule. Thank you for your cooperation and support. Sincerely, Hafsa
